I found two real issues in the markup:

1. **`<script>` placed after `</body>`** — invalid HTML; moves to end of `<body>`  
2. **`aria-live="polite"` on a `hidden` element** (`#success-message`) — content inside a `display:none` / `hidden` element is never announced; announcement is already handled by the always-present `#submit-status` live region, so this attribute is wrong and misleading
data.reasoning_text:
I found the issue: `<script src="form.js">` is placed after `</body>`, which is invalid HTML. The script should be inside `<body>` (typically at the end). Let me fix this.

Also, looking at line 98: `<div id="success-message" class="success-message" hidden aria-live="polite">` - this uses `aria-live="polite"` on an element that starts hidden. The status messages reference says "The live region element must exist in the DOM *before* content is inserted into it" and "Don't hide the live region with `display: none` or `hidden`." 
 
The `hidden` attribute prevents announcements, so the `aria-live="polite"` on the success div is redundant and won't work. But the actual announcements are handled by the `#submit-status` element with `role="status"` that's always in the DOM and visually hidden with `.sr-only`, so that part works fine.

The error paragraphs with `role="alert"` are more problematic—they start hidden with pre-populated content, and when the JS removes the `hidden` attribute after updating the text, screen readers may not re-announce content that was already in the HTML. the element becomes visible with the content already set. Some AT will announce the newly-visible `role="alert"` element, but it's not guaranteed. The spec recommends keeping live regions visible in the DOM and updating their text, rather than hiding them entirely with `hidden`. Axe didn't catch this, and in practice the error is still communicated through the status live region and focus management, but a more robust approach would be using `aria-live` regions that stay in the DOM or hiding with CSS instead.

I'm thinking through the best fix here—using `display: none` via `hidden` for alert elements is problematic, though CSS `visibility: hidden` with height and overflow adjustments would work but adds complexity. The cleanest solution is keeping the error paragraphs always in the DOM but visually hidden when empty, then populating them with content as needed. I should also move the script tag into the body and remove the redundant `aria-live` from the success div since the status region already handles announcements. The simplest solution is to keep the `role="alert"` elements always in the DOM without the `hidden` attribute, starting empty, and just update their text content when errors occur—this way screen readers reliably announce the changes. I could hide them visually with CSS when empty, or just toggle a class to control visibility, but the key is letting the alert element stay present so AT can detect the content change. I can see the main issues to fix: moving the script tag inside the body and removing the redundant `aria-live="polite"` from the hidden success div since the submit status element already handles announcements. Let me apply these corrections and run axe again to verify.
